title: Inference Prescription Journey Mapping — Optimize Recommendations UX
summary: Early-stage wireframe + journey mapping for a compact "prescription" UI inside Optimize that surfaces batching, caching, and quantization suggestions as actionable 'prescriptions' for customers. This doc focuses on interaction flows for mixed-latency workloads and how to present trade-offs (latency vs cost vs error risk) in a concise, scannable way.
problem_statement: ML engineers and platform teams are overwhelmed by long recommendation lists and unclear trade-offs. They need quick, confidence-bearing actions (apply, preview, simulate) that won't break SLAs. Current Recs UI drafts are verbose and don't handle hybrid workloads (low-latency critical routes + high-throughput async routes) cleanly.
goals:
- Reduce time-to-decision for an engineer evaluating cost/perf optimizations.
- Surface only high-confidence prescriptions first, show impact estimates and rollback controls.
- Make it trivial to simulate change impact on historical traces and a small live canary before rolling to all traffic.
- Support mixed-route bundling (grouping changes that should be applied together to avoid incompatibility).
personas:
1) Platform Patty (Platform engineer): cares about throughput, predictable p99, safe rollout.
2) SRE Sam: cares about error modes, tracing, and rollback speed.
3) ML Eng Javier: cares about quality/regression risk and quantization artifacts.

Each persona should be able to get to an 'apply' decision in < 3 clicks for high-confidence recs.
high_level_flow:
1) Overview dashboard: single-line summary card per route/model showing 'Top prescription' (e.g., 'Apply KV caching + 4-bit quantization for this route').
2) Inspect: expands into a compact modal with three tabs: Impact (latency/cost/quality), How it works (short bullets), Simulation (replay historical requests).
3) Preview/canary: two toggles (Preview only, Canary 5% for 30m) with quick estimated impact and safety checks.
4) Apply & verify: Apply creates a rollout plan with auto-fallback on error delta.
5) Audit: post-apply summary card and link to traces/metrics.
wireframe_notes:
- Prescription card (compact): left: icon representing category (batch/cache/quant), center: headline + 2-line rationale, right: three small pills for estimates (cost delta, p50 delta, risk score).
- Hover / expand: first fold shows single-sentence confidence statement (high/medium/low) and top 2 rationale bullets. The modal shows a small timeline chart (latency distribution) + token-cost estimator.
- Simulation tab: allow 'replay sample' where user can select a sample of 100 requests (auto-sampled by error/latency percentiles) and see side-by-side outputs for quality checks (diff highlight).
- Micro-interaction: when user toggles 'Canary', highlight which infra pool will be used, estimated tokens/sec, and immediate circuit-breaker checks (memory/kv-compat).
- Inline help: small 'why this rec' link that opens a short explanation of heuristics (e.g., observed high repeated prefixes => KV cache candidate).
- Visual hierarchy: use color-coded risk badges (green/yellow/red) but never use color alone—include textual 'High confidence' labels.
prioritization_backlog:
Candidate tickets to groom into sprint: 
- OPT-901: 'Replay sample' prototype (backend + UI) for side-by-side output diff.
- OPT-902: Lightweight canary toggle with 1/5/10% presets and 15/30/60 minute windows.
- OPT-905: Risk-scoring microservice to output confidence and failure-mode tips.
- OPT-910: Preset bundling UX for grouping recommended changes (e.g., batch + quantize).
- OPT-914: Metrics panel for simulated costs (historical window selector).
acceptance_criteria:
- Prescription card appears on route-level page with estimated cost and latency deltas.
- Simulation shows a sampled set of requests and side-by-side outputs (basic text diff).
- Canary can be created from the modal and shows live telemetry for the canary cohort.
- Rollout auto-fallback triggers if p99 latency regresses by configured threshold.
- UX passes quick hallway usability test (3 personas, median task completion < 3 minutes).
open_questions: What guardrails do we need for quantization suggestions (auto-revert on quality drift?)
How much historical traffic should be replayed by default for simulation (100, 1k, 10k)?
Should we allow users to edit recommended parameter values (e.g., quant bits) inside the quick modal?
How to surface infrastructure compatibility constraints (e.g., GPU vs CPU pools) without overwhelming users?
decisions_log:
2025-11-07: Keep simulation sample small by default (100 requests) but expose advanced selector for up to 1k.
2025-11-09: Canary defaults: 5% for 30 minutes with explicit rollback threshold setting (p99 +10%).
2025-11-11: First iteration will not allow in-modal editing of quant bits — require 'advanced edit' flow to avoid accidental unsafe combos.
next_steps:
- Build lightweight prototype of the prescription card (UI only) and validate with 3 customers during Nov-Dec design sprint.
- Kick off OPT-901 and OPT-902 in parallel (backend work will overlap).
- Prepare a short demo script and internal checklist for safety review before any canary runs.
- Schedule weekly sync with SRE and Applied ML to iterate on risk heuristics.
